title: Constrictor queue resolution and deferred scaling fixes
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
During a hosted API capacity event on 2026-02-28 we observed prolonged GPU pool exhaustion resulting in long request queue buildup, repeated throttling responses, and noisy autoscaler behaviour. This ticket consolidates the post-incident actions, prioritizes fixes that prevent recurrence, and tracks operational runbook changes.

What happened (short):
- A high-throughput tenant workload with many long-context generation requests triggered aggressive prefetching + KV cache churn.
- Admission logic allowed a burst of requests to enter the pool while autoscaler was in a high-hysteresis window, causing sustained saturation.
- The KV cache eviction pattern caused cache pollution across shards which amplified token compute per-request and increased per-GPU latency, further delaying autoscaler recovery.
- Result: request queue growth, higher latencies, increased 429/503s for some tenants and emergency throttling across pools.

Why this is unique/different from prior tickets:
- Unlike earlier spikes, this incident combined three second-order effects simultaneously: prefetch policy interacting with KV eviction, admission scoring that favoured throughput over tail latency, and autoscaler hysteresis that delayed capacity priming. The triad produced a self-reinforcing queue "constrictor" effect we must break at multiple layers.

Root cause analysis (high level):
- KV cache eviction policy: small-window LRU interactions across tenant-sharded caches resulted in higher miss rates for long-context sequences.
- Prefetch behavior: worker-level prefetch initiated extra keyloading when queues were already growing; prefetches were not admission-gated.
- Admission algorithm: the scoring function allowed many medium-cost requests to enter when slot headroom was essentially already consumed by long requests.
- Autoscaler configuration: scale-up rate limited and cooldown/hysteresis too aggressive for fast transient demand; prewarm didn't trigger due to scale metrics lag.

Immediate mitigations applied (ops):
- Emergency revert of prefetch aggressive flag on 2026-02-28 at 22:12 UTC (rollout rollback link below).
- Temporarily lowered admission window to prefer short requests and enforced per-tenant slot caps.
- Manually primed additional GPU pools for affected regions.

Planned fixes (this ticket scope):
1) KV cache eviction hardening (owner: Priya S) - 3 points - due 2026-03-18
   - Implement age-bucketed eviction to avoid cross-tenant pollution.
   - Add cache miss heatmap telemetry per-shard.
2) Prefetch admission gating (owner: Rohan P) - 2 points - due 2026-03-15
   - Gate prefetch to only run when local queue depth < threshold and global pool pressure low.
   - Add circuit-breaker for worker prefetch during saturation windows.
3) Admission scoring rewrite (owner: Miguel Alvarez) - 5 points - due 2026-03-22
   - Introduce tail-latency penalty into scoring to bias towards requests that lower expected queue tail.
   - Add tenant-priority adjustments and emergency-ejection policy for runaway tenants.
4) Autoscaler tuning and proactive priming (owner: Elena Park) - 3 points - due 2026-03-20
   - Reduce scale-up cooldown for transient spikes and add probe-based rapid-priming flow.
   - Add predictive prewarm job driven by tenant trend model (initially heuristic).
5) Runbook & dashboard updates (owner: SRE team) - 1 point - due 2026-03-12
   - Document emergency steps to roll back prefetch, prime pools, and apply tenant caps.
   - Add Grafana panel linking queue depth, KV miss rate, prefetch activity, and scale events.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Aggressive admission tightening improves tail latency but may reduce throughput; we'll phase in changes behind canary toggles.
- Cache eviction changes add complexity and slightly higher memory usage; acceptable for production stability.
- Autoscaler de-hysteresis reduces spurious scale churn risk; probe-based priming will be rate-limited to avoid oscillation.

Acceptance criteria (for each subtask):
- KV cache: sustained per-shard miss rate drop >= 40% under replayed incident load in staging.
- Prefetch gating: no prefetch started when pool pressure > 70% in chaos testing.
- Admission scoring: synthetic tenants achieve 95th percentile latency improvement vs baseline during contended runs.
- Autoscaler: scale-up time to target capacity reduced by >= 35% in replayed scenario without increasing scale-down flapping.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline and raw traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/incidents/2026-02-28-gpu-exhaustion
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/2026-02-28+GPU+Capacity+Event
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7891 (prefetch-gate), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7905 (kv-eviction-proto), https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/323 (probe-priming)
comments: 2026-03-01 - Avery Chen: Created ticket pulling together action items from postmortem. Triage outcome: prioritize KV eviction + prefetch gating, then admission scoring.
2026-03-02 - Rohan Patel: Deployed prefetch gating feature branch to staging; observed immediate drop in worker keyloads on synthetic replay. PR: runtime#7891.

2026-03-04 - Priya S: Started prototyping age-bucket eviction; initial design adds ~8% memory overhead in staging but reduces cross-shard churn. Linking design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=54321.
2026-03-06 - SRE Ops: Emergency manual priming script documented in runbook; verified pool priming reduces recovery time by ~25% in DR drill.
2026-03-08 - Miguel Alvarez: Admission rewrite design reviewed by Eng and PM; agreed to canary in 2 regions with telemetry gating.
2026-03-10 - Elena Park: Autoscaler probe-priming merged to staging behind feature flag; doing 48h soak before canary to prod.
2026-03-10 - Avery Chen: Updated ticket with owners/due dates. Next step: cut canaries for prefetch gating and KV eviction in low-traffic region (ap-northeast-1) on 2026-03-15.
